topicTitle: NEB Class 11 Physics — Heat and Temperature — 2024
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State and explain the zeroth law of thermodynamics. Why is it called the zeroth law?
questions.solution:
If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.

It is called 'zeroth' because it logically precedes the first and second laws — it was recognised after them but is more fundamental, so it was numbered zero.
questions.knowledgeNote: The zeroth law defines temperature itself and is the basis of all temperature measurement.

questions.question: What is the difference between heat and temperature? Give their SI units.
questions.solution:
**Heat** is energy transferred between systems because of a temperature difference. SI unit: **joule (J)**.

**Temperature** measures the average kinetic energy of the particles — the degree of hotness. SI unit: **kelvin (K)**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Heat is energy in transit; a body contains thermal energy and has a temperature, but it never 'contains heat'.

questions.question: Convert 104°F into the Celsius and Kelvin scales.
questions.knowledgeNote: °F↔°C pivots at −40° (the same number on both scales) — a handy check for conversion arithmetic.

questions.question: What is absolute zero? Why is it unattainable in practice?
questions.solution:
**Absolute zero (0 K = −273.15°C)** is the temperature at which molecular motion is minimal — the zero of the Kelvin scale.

It is unattainable because each cooling step removes a fraction of the remaining thermal energy (third law of thermodynamics): an infinite sequence of steps would be needed to remove it all.
questions.knowledgeNote: The third law: the entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero as T → 0 K — no process can reach 0 K in finite steps.

questions.question: What is the triple point of water? Why is it used to define the Kelvin scale?
questions.solution:
The **triple point of water (273.16 K, 611 Pa)** is the single condition where ice, liquid water, and vapour coexist in equilibrium.

It defines the Kelvin scale (1 K = 1/273.16 of this temperature) because it is a unique, reproducible fixed point — unlike melting or boiling points, it needs no specified pressure.
questions.knowledgeNote: Triple point (273.16 K) vs ice point (273.15 K): the 0.01 K gap is itself an NEB favourite.

questions.question: Body A is in thermal equilibrium with body C, and body B is also in thermal equilibrium with body C. What can you conclude about A and B? Name the law used.
questions.solution:
A and B are in **thermal equilibrium with each other** — they are at the same temperature.

This is the **zeroth law of thermodynamics**, and it is exactly how thermometers work: the thermometer (C) certifies that two bodies share a temperature without them ever touching.
questions.knowledgeNote: Every temperature measurement is a zeroth-law comparison between the object and the thermometer.
